newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD demands EU employment commitment.
newsitem.headline: German SPD demands EU employment commitment.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) vowed on Thursday they would not approve a revised version of the European Union's Maastricht Treaty unless it contained a strong commitment to fighting unemployment.

Heide Wieczorek-Zeul, the party's European affairs spokeswoman, said Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government was trying to water down a new draft version of the treaty, due to be adopted by EU leaders at an Amsterdam summit in June.
"The SPD will not approve the ratification of the revised Maastricht Treaty without the obligation of EU member states to an active employment policy," she told a news conference.
Wieczorek-Zeul also slammed Finance Minister Theo Waigel for linking cuts in social spending with the need to meet the criteria for European Monetary Union (EMU).
"This pulls the support of the population away from European unity," she said. "Nothing is forcing the government to pursue its failed tax and finance policies except its own neo-liberal dogma."
She said the government had also been unclear about whether it would be prepared to accept a postponement of EMU, which is scheduled to begin on January 1, 1999.
"A delay would be the same as at least a temporary failure," she said, predicting a postponent would hit German exporters hard as speculators forced up the price of the deutschemark.
